[Patient]: I'm feeling a bit anxious, to be honest. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping and I just can't seem to relax.
[Doctor]: Hmm, okay. Can you tell me more about what's been going on? When did you first start feeling this way?
[Patient]: It's been about six months now, I think. It just started with feeling a bit on edge all the time, and then it got worse. I have trouble concentrating, and I just feel really worried all the time.
[Doctor]: Yes, okay. Have you experienced any other symptoms like chest pain or shortness of breath?
[Patient]: No, nothing like that. Just feeling really anxious and worried all the time. And I have trouble sleeping.
[Doctor]: Alright. And have you noticed any triggers that make you feel more anxious?
[Patient]: Yeah, I guess just everyday things. Like, I'll be worried about work, or my family, or just little things that wouldn't used to bother me.
[Doctor]: I see. And have you tried any ways to manage your anxiety, like exercise or meditation?
[Patient]: Yeah, I've tried to exercise a bit more, but it's hard to motivate myself when I'm feeling so anxious.
[Doctor]: Okay, that's understandable. Let's take a look at your blood pressure and heart rate, okay? Your blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, and your heart rate is 100 beats per minute.
[Patient]: Okay...
[Doctor]: (after taking the blood pressure and heart rate) Your blood pressure is a bit elevated, and your heart rate is also a bit faster than normal. But that's consistent with anxiety.
[Patient]: Okay, what does that mean?
[Doctor]: It means that your anxiety is probably contributing to your elevated blood pressure and heart rate. But don't worry, we can work with that. I'm going to diagnose you with Generalized Anxiety Disorder.
[Patient]: Okay, good.
[Doctor]: Now, I'd like to prescribe you some medication to help manage your anxiety. Have you ever taken any medications for anxiety before?
[Patient]: No, I haven't.
[Doctor]: Okay, well, I'm going to prescribe you a medication called Sertraline, 50mg oral tablets, once daily. It's an SSRI, and it should help with your anxiety symptoms.
[Patient]: Okay, sounds good.
[Doctor]: And I'd also like you to follow up with me in two weeks to assess response to treatment and adjust as necessary. And in the meantime, I want you to try to practice some relaxation techniques, like deep breathing, and try to exercise a bit more regularly.
[Patient]: Okay, that sounds like a plan.
[Doctor]: Yes, okay. And if your symptoms worsen or don't improve, we may need to consider referring you to a psychiatrist for further evaluation.
[Patient]: Okay, I understand.
[Doctor]: Alright, let's get you set up with the medication and the follow-up appointment, okay? I'll have my nurse come in and go over the medication instructions with you.
[Patient]: Sounds good, thank you.
[Doctor]: You're welcome. Take care, and I'll see you in two weeks.
